title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Sales Tax Bulletin — Crediting Back Tax Charged on Exempt Purchases
content:
Sales tax charged on a Ridgeline Pro Credit invoice is credited back in full when the purchase was exempt.

## When a purchase was exempt

A purchase was exempt when the account had an exemption certificate whose effective date is on or before the invoice date and whose expiry date is on or after the invoice date, and the tier allows tax-exempt purchases. A certificate placed on file after the purchase covers that purchase only when its effective date is on or before the invoice date; a certificate that took effect later never covers it.

| Certificate effective date | Certificate expiry date | Covers an invoice dated 20 April? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 January | 31 December | Yes |
| 20 April | 31 December | Yes — effective on the invoice date |
| 1 January | 20 April | Yes — valid through the invoice date |
| 21 April (placed on file in May) | 31 December | No — took effect after the invoice date |
| 1 January (placed on file in May) | 31 December | Yes — effective before the invoice date |

## Request window

The credit must be requested no later than the tier's sales tax credit look-back days, in calendar days, after the invoice date. Days are counted as calendar days from the invoice date as day 0 to the date of the request; a request on the last day qualifies and a later one does not. The invoice date is the one on the invoice record.

Hypothetical pair on a 90-day tier, invoice dated 1 March: day 90 falls on 30 May, so a request on 30 May qualifies and one on 31 May does not.

## Amount and limit

The credit equals the invoice's sales tax less any part of that tax already credited by a return credit, and an invoice receives at most one tax credit, as shown by the tax credits already referencing it.

Hypothetical example: an exempt invoice charged 420.00 of sales tax, and a return credit on that invoice has already given back 60.00 of tax; the tax credit is 360.00.
